coverage_note: 00:00-06:40 is English admin talk about the verb-collocation list (no Arabic practice). 06:40-16:40 free talk (woke up late, lazy morning, trip to uncle, camping). 16:54-1:03:48 is a rule lesson on the tool words awal / taani / aa5er / 8eir / nafs / kul and el-: most Medi turns there are meta-questions about the rule in English or Latin-letter Arabic (17:31-17:53 'awal saa', 57:38-59:49 'awwal marra, tani marra, nafs il ishi'), which I did not score as uses or slips per the brief. Several of Amal's fixes in that block fit no bucket (tool word + el- flips the meaning: awal el-saa3a = beginning of the hour, taani el-saa3a = nothing, 8eir never takes el-, nafs always does) - filed as PROPOSE with one rule line; the after-the-noun adjective fixes (el-saa3a el-oola, el-marra el-a5eera, el-yoam el-awal) are A7/A8. Echo check: echo-candidates has one candidate 14:26 'Forgot it all.' - real English, not an echo. take_verb empty. laazem_noun 09:38 'أنا لازم عطلة' -> Amal 'لازم you should take' = B2 row (GR-27). Engine: 07:02 wrote سمعت - Amal's echo صحيت and chat 's7eet' show he said sme3et for s7eet (counted, GR-24); 07:54 'كان قنيش' is noise around كان; 43:20 engine wrote هذا الثاني - Amal's echo حدا التاني is what he said; 1:04:01 Amal's 'شوفك' is most likely بشوفك with the b- lost by the engine. Not counted: 07:38 على العشرة = repeat of the line Amal just fixed (GR-28); 08:17 في الصباح / 08:20 الصباح - Amal said both are fine; 10:43 أنا خططت self-fix (GR-22); 16:09 تنتين و تلت self-fix; 31:28 'the second car -> the first car' self-fix; 45:35 العشر دقايق he doubted himself but was right; 49:04 'every day' in English then his own 'Is it كل يوم?' before she spoke (self-fix, kul yoam is on her sheet); 51:15 'hadi / hada nafs el-ishi?' is a question about the rule; 59:54 'نفس إشي' Amal's reply ('Or existing. It does.') is unclear, not scored. Pronunciation (S4) left out: 09:23 متشجاع vowel stretch (the word fix شجاع->متشجع is counted).

rows.proposed_rule: Tool words and el-: awal / aa5er + bare noun = first / last X, awal / aa5er + el-noun = the beginning / end of X; taani and 8eir never take el- on the next noun (taani saa3a, 8eir yoam) and 'another X' is X + taani after the noun; nafs always takes el- after it (nafs el-ishi).
